Decision-audit for an autocuda run on `linalg/qr_v2` (batched square Householder QR, B200). Read-only, no edits. Be rigorous. <=260 words.

The fleet has EXHAUSTIVELY floored the current n512 kernel: panel (47% of n512) is a serial scalar Householder formation (architecturally irreducible — 4 briefs); trailing (53%) is tf32x3i-optimized at its roofline. The panel and trailing run as SEPARATE sequential kernel launches in a ~16-iteration outer loop (one panel + one trailing per outer block). Best = 2470us, gap to #1 (1333us) is structural.

PROPOSED BIG IDEA for worker 1: a WARP-SPECIALIZED PERSISTENT megakernel for n512 (one persistent CTA per matrix, or a persistent grid) that OVERLAPS panel(k+1) with trailing(k) — producer warps factor the next panel on the columns it needs while consumer warps do the current trailing on the remaining columns — synchronized by NAMED BARRIERS (bar.sync / mbarrier), NOT separate CUDA streams (streams are leaderboard-REJECTED). The thesis: this hides the panel's serial latency behind the trailing's tensor-core work, breaking the panel+trailing SEQUENTIAL-PHASE floor that separate launches can't.

CRITICAL QUESTIONS — verify against the worker logs (autocuda/2026-06-22-09-10-03-qr_v2-optimize-tree-worker-*-log.csv):
1. Was this EXACT idea already BUILT and measured? Grep for "megakernel", "warp-speciali[sz]", "look-ahead", "lookahead", "persistent", "producer", "brief-7", "brief-25", "qr_mega". Distinguish: (a) W0 brief-7 reportedly built a megakernel that lost 8.6x — was it the NAIVE 1-block-per-matrix fusion (occupancy-walled), or the warp-specialized producer-consumer PIPELINE? (b) W2 brief-25 reportedly DESIGNED a "persistent warp-specialized look-ahead megakernel" but it was "NOT built" — confirm whether it was ever actually implemented+benchmarked or only deferred.
2. Is the thesis sound that overlapping panel(k+1)∥trailing(k) within a persistent CTA can win at n512 B=640, given: at B=640 the batch already SATURATES the 148 SMs (so a persistent-CTA-per-matrix has no spare SMs to overlap into — the GPU is already full of independent matrices' work)? Or does saturation kill the overlap benefit (the trailing of matrix i already overlaps the panel of matrix j across the batch via the scheduler)? THIS IS THE CRUX: at B=640 >> 148 SMs, is there ANY idle resource for intra-matrix look-ahead to capture, or is cross-matrix batch parallelism already doing it?
3. If it can't win at saturated n512 (B=640), could it win at n1024 (B=60 < 148 SMs, grid-UNDER-filled, ~88 idle SMs during the panel phase) where there IS spare capacity?

End with: VERDICT: VIABLE (which shape, why the saturation argument doesn't kill it) or DEAD (the saturation/already-built reason). Be decisive — this is a multi-hour build, so only greenlight if there's a real mechanism.
